get.description: The caller's passkeys, newest first (revoked ones included), and `stepUp`: the step-up mode of the caller's tenant (`log`: recorded, `enforce`: required before a policy set is published or rolled back to, and before one's passkeys change) and whether passkeys are available on this platform. Every role but the End User (403 `PASSKEY_NOT_AVAILABLE`), and the End User too once the platform allows it (not by default); 503 `PASSKEYS_NOT_CONFIGURED` when the platform has no relying party.

deviceType.description: multiDevice: a synced passkey (a password manager or a platform's keychain); singleDevice: bound to one authenticator

423.description: Default Response

post.description: The authenticator's answer to the registration's options (`credential`: the RegistrationResponseJSON — `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON()`), verified against its challenge, the relying party its options named and that relying party's origins, with user verification. A credential is registered once; at most ten active passkeys. Refusals: 400 `PASSKEY_CHALLENGE_INVALID`, `PASSKEY_REGISTRATION_INVALID`, `PASSKEY_NAME_INVALID`; 403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `STEP_UP_INVALID`; 409 `PASSKEY_IN_USE`, `PASSKEY_LIMIT`. Every role but the End User (403 `PASSKEY_NOT_AVAILABLE`), and the End User too once the platform allows it (not by default); 503 `PASSKEYS_NOT_CONFIGURED` when the platform has no relying party.

stepUpToken.description: A step-up token for this action (POST /v1/auth/step-up), when the caller already has a passkey: under the tenant's step-up mode `enforce` it is required (403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `STEP_UP_INVALID`); under `log` a missing or wrong one is recorded and nothing is refused.

deviceType.description: multiDevice: a synced passkey (a password manager or a platform's keychain); singleDevice: bound to one authenticator

423.description: Default Response

post.description: The options for `navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey })` (the WebAuthn JSON form: decode `challenge` and `user.id` from base64url), and `ceremonyId`, which the answer names (POST /v1/auth/passkeys). Five minutes, once. Attestation none, user verification required. `stepUpAction` is `passkey.register` when the caller has a passkey already: the new one is then confirmed with one of theirs. `rpId` names the relying party (your tenant's passkey address); absent, Aurea's own. Every role but the End User (403 `PASSKEY_NOT_AVAILABLE`), and the End User too once the platform allows it (not by default); 503 `PASSKEYS_NOT_CONFIGURED` when the platform has no relying party.

schema.description: Optional: send no body for Aurea's own relying party.

rpId.description: The relying party id the options are for: your tenant's passkey address (`rpId` of GET /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/passkey-address), for your own app's passkeys; absent, Aurea's own. Any other: 400 `PASSKEY_RP_NOT_ALLOWED`.

requestBody.description: Optional: send no body for Aurea's own relying party.

423.description: Default Response

post.description: One of the caller's passkeys, revoked for good. Refusals: 404 `PASSKEY_NOT_FOUND`; 409 `PASSKEY_REVOKED`; 403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `STEP_UP_INVALID`. Every role but the End User (403 `PASSKEY_NOT_AVAILABLE`), and the End User too once the platform allows it (not by default); 503 `PASSKEYS_NOT_CONFIGURED` when the platform has no relying party.

stepUpToken.description: A step-up token for this action (POST /v1/auth/step-up), when the caller already has a passkey: under the tenant's step-up mode `enforce` it is required (403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `STEP_UP_INVALID`); under `log` a missing or wrong one is recorded and nothing is refused.

deviceType.description: multiDevice: a synced passkey (a password manager or a platform's keychain); singleDevice: bound to one authenticator

423.description: Default Response

post.summary: Start a step-up for one action
post.description: The options for `navigator.credentials.get({ publicKey })` (decode `challenge` and each `allowCredentials[].id` from base64url) for one action on one target — the challenge commits to it — and `ceremonyId`. Actions: `approval.approve` and `approval.reject` {operationId} (an approver of the caller's tenant: the operation's newest approval request and its canonical payload for that action), `policy_set.publish` and `policy_set.rollback` {setId} (`tenant.policies.write`; a platform role names {tenantId}), `passkey.register` {} and `passkey.revoke` {passkeyId} (one's own), `agent_execution.approve` and `agent_execution.reject` {executionId} (an approver of the tenant's agent payments, on one of its agent payments). `rpId` names the relying party (your tenant's passkey address); absent, Aurea's own — only the caller's passkeys of that relying party may answer. Refusals: 400 `STEP_UP_ACTION_INVALID`, `PASSKEY_RP_NOT_ALLOWED`; 403 `STEP_UP_ACTION_FORBIDDEN`; 404 `STEP_UP_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`; 409 `STEP_UP_NO_PASSKEY`. Every role but the End User (403 `PASSKEY_NOT_AVAILABLE`), and the End User too once the platform allows it (not by default); 503 `PASSKEYS_NOT_CONFIGURED` when the platform has no relying party.

rpId.description: The relying party id the options are for: your tenant's passkey address (`rpId` of GET /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/passkey-address), for your own app's passkeys; absent, Aurea's own. Any other: 400 `PASSKEY_RP_NOT_ALLOWED`.

423.description: Default Response

post.summary: Confirm a step-up with a passkey
post.description: The assertion that answers the step-up's options (`credential`: the AuthenticationResponseJSON), verified with the caller's passkey it names — one of the relying party its options named — (user verification, its counter, its signature over the challenge). Answers `stepUpToken`: two minutes, used once, by the caller, for that action on that target only — send it with the action (`stepUpToken`). Refusal: 403 `STEP_UP_INVALID` (unknown, used or expired options, another passkey, a signature that does not verify). Every role but the End User (403 `PASSKEY_NOT_AVAILABLE`), and the End User too once the platform allows it (not by default); 503 `PASSKEYS_NOT_CONFIGURED` when the platform has no relying party.

423.description: Default Response

post.summary: Start a threshold signing ceremony for an MPC wallet (DEVICE+AUREA, or BACKUP recovery)

committee.description: The two parties that sign: DEVICE and AUREA (the default), or BACKUP and AUREA (a signature from the backup, after a lost device), which may need the owner's step-up (`stepUpToken` or `password`).

msgHashHex.description: The digest to sign, hex (an optional 0x prefix).

wireVersion.description: The relay version the client speaks: 2, or 1 where the tenant is still allowed version 1. Omitted: 1.

rosterStatement.description: Ask Aurea's cosigner for its signed roster statement, which the client checks against the cosigner's pinned identity key before it sends anything (relay version 2). Omitted: no statement.

intent.description: What the digest signs, decoded (an EIP-1559 transaction, EIP-712 typed data, an EIP-191 message, or a backup proof), by its `kind`: it is checked against the digest before the signature is given.

approval.description: The wallet approval key's approval of this digest, for a wallet with a bound approval key (dkg/start `approvalBinding`): `{"alg":"webauthn-es256","credentialId","authenticatorData","clientDataJSON","signature"}` (base64url), or `{"alg":"p256-raw","signature"}` (r ‖ s, base64url), over the challenge SHA-256("aurea-mpc-approval/v1" 0x00 ‖ lp16(walletId) ‖ digest). Aurea's cosigner verifies it.

stepUpToken.description: A BACKUP committee, where the owner's step-up is required: the owner's passkey step-up token for this signature.

password.description: A BACKUP committee, where the owner's step-up is required: the owner's current password, instead of `stepUpToken`.

presignIds.description: A version 3 wallet: the ids of the presignatures the client holds for it (at most 16); the signature may use one of them.

holdId.description: The retry of a payment the wallet's co-signing policy held: the hold's id.

riskAcknowledged.description: Where the platform has the transaction risk preview on: the `simulationId` of the preview whose risk the user acknowledged before the passkey (recorded; never required).

schema.description: The digest to sign and what it is. Unknown members are ignored.

requestBody.description: The digest to sign and what it is. Unknown members are ignored.

simulation.description: Where the platform has the transaction risk preview on and the signature carries an EIP-1559 or EIP-712 `intent`: the preview it stands on, as POST /v1/transactions/simulate answers it; absent otherwise

post.summary: Prepare a backup proof: its message, for the user's approval
post.description: A wallet with a bound approval key signs nothing without the user's approval of the digest, a backup proof included. This answers the message a proof will sign, its digest, the intent (`backup_proof`) and a token (valid until `expiresAt`); nothing is written and the cosigner is not asked. The client approves the digest with the wallet's approval key and starts the proof with `prepared` and `approval`. Only where the backup proof's approval is on (otherwise 404 BACKUP_PROOF_PREPARE_OFF: start the proof without it).

post.description: The client proves it holds the wallet's backup share: the Hub issues a challenge (valid ten minutes, used once) and a relay session whose parties are BACKUP and AUREA only — the device share cannot take part — and asks the cosigner to join it. post.summary: Auth bridge — issue a scoped MPC Hub JWT for a first-party app's merchant
post.description:
Lets an authenticated first-party app (e.g. the aurea-pay payment-link product) obtain a short-lived Hub JWT for ONE of its merchants, so that merchant's browser can drive an MPC ceremony through `/v1/mpc/relay/*` + the live AUREA cosigner WITHOUT being a hand-created Hub user. This is the integration entry point for any external client.

**Auth:** the existing tenant-HMAC scheme — send `x-tenant-api-key`, `x-timestamp`, and `x-signature` = HMAC-SHA256(apiSecret, `METHOD\nPATH\nTIMESTAMP\nSHA256(rawBody)`), ±300s window. The call runs under that tenant; the merchant is find-or-created beneath it, keyed deterministically by `externalMerchantId` (same id → same Hub user → same wallet).

**Request body:** `{ externalMerchantId: string }` (≤80 chars); optional `scopes: ["ramp"]`: where moving an app's accounts to the Hub is switched on, a scoped token also reaches the bank ramp's user routes (`/v1/ramp/bank/payin/*`, `/v1/ramp/bank/customer/*`).

**Response 200:** `{ accessToken, expiresIn, sub, tenantId }` — a short-lived HS256 JWT `{ sub, tenantId, role:'user' }` accepted unchanged by the relay `authenticate`/`relayAuth` hooks.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Optional (required for institutional tenants). Up to 255 letters, digits, - or _. Sending the same key again with the same request answers with the first answer instead of running it again, and the response carries idempotency-replayed: true. The same key with a different request, or while the first call is still running, answers 409 with details.code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED or IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS; after a first call that may have taken effect without answering, 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (it is never run again: check the operation, then use a new key). A key that is not one answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID. A request without the header behaves as it always has. Keys last 24 hours.

parameters.name: x-external-tx-id
parameters.description: Optional. Your own id for the operation this call starts: up to 255 letters, digits, and - _ . : — unique for your tenant for ever. The operation keeps it (externalTxId) and GET /v1/operations/by-external-id/{externalTxId} finds it. An id another operation of your tenant already holds answers 409 with details.code EXTERNAL_TX_ID_REUSED and details.operationId, before anything is signed or sent; an id that is not one answers 400 EXTERNAL_TX_ID_INVALID. A call refused before it recorded an operation (a validation error, say) leaves the id free. With an Idempotency-Key, the same key and the same id answer the first answer again. Honoured once Aurea records your operations (GET /v1/operations lists them); until then the header is not read. A request without it behaves as it always has.

post.description: Request a quote for swapping tokens through Aurea's swap router. Supports both mainnet (default) and testnet operations via the isTestnet parameter. Returns estimated gas costs in user-friendly format (native tokens) if available. Balance validation fields (transactionValueNative, totalCostRequired, sufficientBalance, nativeTokenBalance) help determine if user has sufficient funds. Gas cost fields (estimatedGasCostWei, estimatedGasCostNative, nativeTokenSymbol) are optional and omitted if gas price fetch fails.

estimatedGas.description: Estimated gas units for the transaction

estimatedGasCostWei.description: Estimated gas cost in Wei (smallest unit). Omitted if gas price fetch fails.

estimatedGasCostNative.description: Estimated gas cost in native tokens (e.g., '0.046386660' MATIC). Omitted if gas price fetch fails.

nativeTokenSymbol.description: Symbol of the FROM chain's native token (e.g., 'MATIC', 'ETH'). Omitted if gas price fetch fails.

nativeTokenBalance.description: User's balance of native token on FROM chain (e.g., '2.766'). Omitted if balance fetch fails.

transactionValueNative.description: Transaction value in native token format (e.g., '2.31' MATIC). For cross-chain swaps, this includes swap amount + destination gas fees + bridge fees. This is the amount that will be deducted from your wallet as the transaction value. Omitted if gas price fetch fails.

totalCostRequired.description: Total cost required for the swap in native tokens (transactionValueNative + estimatedGasCostNative). This is the total amount you need in your wallet to execute the swap. Omitted if gas price fetch fails.

sufficientBalance.description: Whether the user has sufficient balance to cover the total cost. True if nativeTokenBalance >= totalCostRequired. Omitted if balance unavailable or gas fetch fails.

sourceChainType.description: Whether the source chain is EVM or Solana. Determines the execution path on the client.

isTestnet.description: Indicates if the quote is for a testnet network.

fromChainId.description: Resolved numeric chain ID for the source network.

toChainId.description: Resolved numeric chain ID for the destination network.

requiresDestinationSignature.description: Always false in current responses — routes requiring a second signature on the destination chain are rejected server-side.

gasless.description: Gasless swap metadata. Present when the swap can be executed via EIP-712 permit (e.g. EUR.e → the chain's native token). Null when gasless is not supported for this route.

supported.description: Whether gasless execution is supported for this quote.

permitRequired.description: Whether an EIP-2612 permit signature is required (true when current allowance is insufficient).

estimatedGasCost.description: Estimated gas cost in the from-chain native token.

estimatedGasCostXDAI.description: Estimated gas cost, in the chain's native token.

currentNonce.description: Current ERC-2612 permit nonce for the wallet.

permitDomain.description: EIP-712 domain parameters used to build the permit signature.

post.summary: Start the user's authorization on the bank ramp's pages
post.description: For a tenant whose KYC goes through the bank ramp's own pages: answers the URL to send the user to, where they sign up, complete their KYC and grant the tenant's application access. The bank ramp then sends the user back to `redirectUri` (one the tenant's application registered with it) with `code` and `state`: hand both to POST /v1/ramp/bank/customer/authorize/complete. The PKCE verifier stays with Aurea; the `state` is signed, names this user and request, is used once and lasts a day (`expiresAt`). `redirectUri` is an https URL, http to the local machine, or an app's own scheme, without a fragment (400 `BANK_RAMP_REDIRECT_URI_INVALID` otherwise). The tenant's bank ramp KYC must be on in the environment (403 `BANK_RAMP_FUNCTION_OFF`) with the hosted strategy (403 `BANK_RAMP_KYC_STRATEGY_OFF`), and its bank ramp configured with an authorization client (503 `BANK_RAMP_NOT_CONFIGURED`). A token without a tenant answers 403.

post.summary: Link one of the user's Aurea wallets to the customer
post.description: The bank ramp takes payments to and from an address on a chain once the address signed its message. A custodial wallet is signed for by Aurea and linked at once (201); a client-side or MPC wallet's link waits for the wallet's signature of `message` (202): send it to POST /v1/ramp/bank/customer/wallets/{linkId}/signature within `expiresAt`. A live link for the wallet's address on that chain is answered as it is (200). The wallet must be the user's (404 `BANK_RAMP_WALLET_NOT_FOUND`), of the environment, an EVM account that can sign — not watch-only, not a contract wallet (409 `BANK_RAMP_WALLET_NOT_SIGNABLE`, with the `reason`). A frozen tenant, user or wallet answers 423. The tenant must have the bank ramp's Aurea wallets mode on in the environment (403 `BANK_RAMP_MODE_OFF`) and offer the chain (400 `BANK_RAMP_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE`); the user must be a customer of the bank ramp (404 `BANK_RAMP_CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND`). A token without a tenant answers 403. An optional `Idempotency-Key` header answers a repeated call with the first call's answer.

isTestnet.description: The bank ramp's environment: true for sandbox, false or omitted for production.

signer.description: server: Aurea signed with the wallet's key (a custodial wallet); client: the wallet's own device or MPC ceremony signs.

status.description: awaiting_signature: sign `message` (its EIP-191 digest is `digest`) and send the signature; linked: the bank ramp takes payments to and from this address on this chain; pending: the bank ramp is still checking; failed: refused (`failureCode`); expired: link the wallet again.

post.summary: Ask for the challenge that proves an address of the user
post.description: An address outside Aurea is proven twice: it signs `message` (Aurea's challenge: the tenant, the user, the address, the environment, a nonce, ten minutes) and `linkMessage` (the bank ramp's own message). Send both signatures to POST /v1/ramp/bank/customer/addresses/verify. An EVM address with its checksum when mixed-case (400 `BANK_RAMP_ADDRESS_INVALID`); at most five open challenges per user (409 `BANK_RAMP_ADDRESS_CHALLENGE_LIMIT`). The tenant must have the bank ramp's standalone mode on in the environment (403 `BANK_RAMP_MODE_OFF`) and offer the chain (400 `BANK_RAMP_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE`); the user must be a customer of the bank ramp (404 `BANK_RAMP_CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND`). A token without a tenant answers 403.

post.summary: Prove an address of the user and link it
post.description: `signature`: the address's signature of the challenge's `message` — an account's (personal_sign) or a smart account's (ERC-1271, checked on the chain). `linkSignature`: its signature of `linkMessage` the same ways, or `0x` for a smart account that signs on chain. Both are checked before anything reaches the bank ramp: a wrong one answers 400 `BANK_RAMP_ADDRESS_SIGNATURE_INVALID` (`signature`: challenge or link); five wrong challenge signatures spend the challenge. 201 linked, 202 pending (a smart account's on-chain signature: list the addresses to read it again), 200 when the customer had the address on that chain already. A challenge used, expired or spent answers 409 `BANK_RAMP_ADDRESS_CHALLENGE_SPENT`. A smart account's signatures are read through the chain's node (503 `BANK_RAMP_ADDRESS_UNVERIFIED` when it does not answer).

post.description: 201 with the endpoint and its secret, shown once. `url` must be https on the default port and name a public DNS host; `eventTypes` lists the types it receives (empty: the ramp.* and earn.* types only; operation.*, tokenized_asset.* and every type published later only when named); `description` is the tenant's own label; `status` defaults to active. A refused value answers 400 with `details.code` WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_INVALID, `details.field` and, for the address, `details.reason`; an eleventh endpoint in one environment 409 WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_LIMIT. Each delivery is a POST with the JSON body `{ id, type, environment, occurredAt, createdAt, data }` (published per type as the components `WebhookEvent.<type>.v<version>`) and the headers `x-webhook-id`, `x-webhook-timestamp`, `x-webhook-event` and `x-webhook-signature: v1=<base64 HMAC-SHA256>` of `<id>.<timestamp>.<body>`, keyed with the bytes of the base64 after `whsec_`. When Aurea signs its deliveries, `x-webhook-jws` adds a detached JWS (ES256) of the exact body: put the base64url of the raw body between its two dots and verify it with GET /v1/webhooks/jwks.json; its protected header names the key (`kid`), the tenant (`aud`), the attempt's time (`iat`) and the event (`jti`). Answer 2xx within 10 seconds; anything else is retried for up to 10 attempts. The same event reaches every address that asks for it with the same `id`. No order is promised between deliveries.

post.description: Sends one `webhook.test` delivery now, signed like every other, whether the endpoint is active or not, and answers what happened: `delivered` is true for a 2xx. Not queued, not retried, not in the log of attempts, and at most 10 a minute. 404 WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND. Each delivery is a POST with the JSON body `{ id, type, environment, occurredAt, createdAt, data }` (published per type as the components `WebhookEvent.<type>.v<version>`) and the headers `x-webhook-id`, `x-webhook-timestamp`, `x-webhook-event` and `x-webhook-signature: v1=<base64 HMAC-SHA256>` of `<id>.<timestamp>.<body>`, keyed with the bytes of the base64 after `whsec_`. When Aurea signs its deliveries, `x-webhook-jws` adds a detached JWS (ES256) of the exact body: put the base64url of the raw body between its two dots and verify it with GET /v1/webhooks/jwks.json; its protected header names the key (`kid`), the tenant (`aud`), the attempt's time (`iat`) and the event (`jti`). Answer 2xx within 10 seconds; anything else is retried for up to 10 attempts. The same event reaches every address that asks for it with the same `id`. No order is promised between deliveries.

state.description: SUBMITTED → PENDING_SCREENING → PENDING_ENRICHMENT → PENDING_POLICY → PENDING_AUTHORIZATION → QUEUED → PENDING_SIGNATURE → SIGNED → BROADCASTING → CONFIRMING → COMPLETED; or CANCELLING, CANCELLED, BLOCKED, REJECTED, FAILED. COMPLETED, CANCELLED, BLOCKED, REJECTED and FAILED are final. A state only moves forward.

subState.description: Where within its state the operation is. PENDING_SCREENING/not_gated: Passed without a screening that can stop it: none is enforced for its tenant. PENDING_SCREENING/screened: Screened before anything was signed (the screening enforced for its tenant): it went on because nothing matched, or a match was released by the tenant's review. PENDING_SCREENING/under_review: Held for the tenant's compliance review before anything is signed or sent: it goes on if released, and ends REJECTED if not. PENDING_SCREENING/bypassed: Released by the tenant's compliance review: it goes on as the call that started it would have. PENDING_ENRICHMENT/not_gated: Passed without a decoding or a simulation that can stop it: none is enforced for its tenant (where the simulation runs in log, its outcome is recorded with the operation, `simulations`). PENDING_ENRICHMENT/simulated: Decoded and simulated before anything was signed (the simulation enforced for its tenant): it went on because the outcome kept to what was asked. An outcome that diverged, or a transaction that could not be simulated, ended it FAILED (not_sent) with TX_SIMULATION_DIVERGES or TX_NOT_SIMULATED. PENDING_POLICY/not_gated: Passed without a policy that can stop it: no policy is enforced yet. PENDING_POLICY/evaluated: Evaluated by the tenant's policy, which is enforced (an institutional tenant): the verdict decides what follows. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/not_gated: Passed without an approval: none is asked for yet. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/not_required: Passed without an approval: the tenant's policy allowed it as it is. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/awaiting_approval: Held for approval by the tenant's policy (an institutional tenant): nothing is signed or sent until the rule's approvers approve it (GET /v1/operations/{id}/approval). PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/approved: Approved by the rule's threshold of approvers: it goes on as the call that started it would have. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/awaiting_callback: Held by the tenant's own callback, which answered RETRY (an institutional tenant, where the institution's callback is on): nothing is signed or sent; Aurea asks the callback again until its deadline (48 hours at most) and the operation goes on as the call that started it would have once it approves. QUEUED/not_gated: Passed without a queue of its own: the wallet's nonce is taken as before. PENDING_SIGNATURE/awaiting_client_signature: Handed to the user's device (or MPC) to sign: what it signs comes back with the broadcast. PENDING_SIGNATURE/signing: Signed by Aurea for the wallet it holds the key of. SIGNED/signed_by_client: Signed on the user's side. SIGNED/signed_by_hub: Signed by Aurea. BROADCASTING/sending: Being handed to the chain's node, or to the provider. BROADCASTING/outcome_unknown: Handed over without an answer: it may still go through, and is never sent again by itself. CONFIRMING/awaiting_confirmation: On its way on chain, waiting for its receipt. CONFIRMING/awaiting_provider: Accepted by the provider, which has not settled it yet. CONFIRMING/awaiting_delivery: A swap mined on its source chain, which the router has not delivered yet (a cross-chain or intent swap; followed only where delivery tracking is switched on). CONFIRMING/awaiting_finalization: A Solana transaction the cluster confirmed, waiting to be finalized (followed only where the operations reconciliation runs); its answer and its transaction already say confirmed. CONFIRMING/confirming: Mined, and waiting until its chain has built the platform's confirmations for that chain on it (followed only where the confirmations are switched on). CONFIRMING/reorged: Its block left the chain in a reorganisation: the same signed transaction was handed to the node again, and it waits to be mined again. CONFIRMING/sped_up: Its transaction was replaced by the same one at the same nonce with a higher fee (POST /v1/operations/{id}/speed-up): whichever of them is mined ends it. COMPLETED/confirmed: Mined and successful. COMPLETED/processed: Settled by the provider. COMPLETED/signed: A signature, not a transaction: the message or digest is signed, and nothing is sent on chain. COMPLETED/delivered: A swap the router delivered as quoted. COMPLETED/delivered_other_token: A swap the router delivered in another token than the one quoted (a partial route). CANCELLING/drop_sent: A 0-value transaction to the wallet itself was sent at its transaction's nonce with a higher fee (POST /v1/operations/{id}/drop): CANCELLED if it is mined, COMPLETED or FAILED if the original is. FAILED/not_sent: Refused or failed before anything was signed or sent. FAILED/submission_failed: Sending it failed: the node or the provider refused it, or did not take it. FAILED/reverted: Mined, and reverted. FAILED/never_broadcast: Never signed and sent back within an hour: it can no longer be broadcast. FAILED/provider_rejected: Refused by the provider after it took the order. FAILED/delivery_failed: A swap mined on its source chain that the router reports failed on the way. FAILED/refunded: A swap the router could not deliver and refunded on the source chain. FAILED/approval_expired: Held for approval, and not approved within the approval window: nothing was signed or sent. FAILED/callback_expired: Held for the tenant's callback, which did not approve it before its deadline: nothing was signed or sent. FAILED/dropped: Its block left the chain in a reorganisation, and another transaction of the wallet took its nonce: it can never be mined.

state.description: SUBMITTED → PENDING_SCREENING → PENDING_ENRICHMENT → PENDING_POLICY → PENDING_AUTHORIZATION → QUEUED → PENDING_SIGNATURE → SIGNED → BROADCASTING → CONFIRMING → COMPLETED; or CANCELLING, CANCELLED, BLOCKED, REJECTED, FAILED. COMPLETED, CANCELLED, BLOCKED, REJECTED and FAILED are final. A state only moves forward.

subState.description: Where within its state the operation is. PENDING_SCREENING/not_gated: Passed without a screening that can stop it: none is enforced for its tenant. PENDING_SCREENING/screened: Screened before anything was signed (the screening enforced for its tenant): it went on because nothing matched, or a match was released by the tenant's review. PENDING_SCREENING/under_review: Held for the tenant's compliance review before anything is signed or sent: it goes on if released, and ends REJECTED if not. PENDING_SCREENING/bypassed: Released by the tenant's compliance review: it goes on as the call that started it would have. PENDING_ENRICHMENT/not_gated: Passed without a decoding or a simulation that can stop it: none is enforced for its tenant (where the simulation runs in log, its outcome is recorded with the operation, `simulations`). PENDING_ENRICHMENT/simulated: Decoded and simulated before anything was signed (the simulation enforced for its tenant): it went on because the outcome kept to what was asked. An outcome that diverged, or a transaction that could not be simulated, ended it FAILED (not_sent) with TX_SIMULATION_DIVERGES or TX_NOT_SIMULATED. PENDING_POLICY/not_gated: Passed without a policy that can stop it: no policy is enforced yet. PENDING_POLICY/evaluated: Evaluated by the tenant's policy, which is enforced (an institutional tenant): the verdict decides what follows. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/not_gated: Passed without an approval: none is asked for yet. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/not_required: Passed without an approval: the tenant's policy allowed it as it is. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/awaiting_approval: Held for approval by the tenant's policy (an institutional tenant): nothing is signed or sent until the rule's approvers approve it (GET /v1/operations/{id}/approval). PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/approved: Approved by the rule's threshold of approvers: it goes on as the call that started it would have. PENDING_AUTHORIZATION/awaiting_callback: Held by the tenant's own callback, which answered RETRY (an institutional tenant, where the institution's callback is on): nothing is signed or sent; Aurea asks the callback again until its deadline (48 hours at most) and the operation goes on as the call that started it would have once it approves. QUEUED/not_gated: Passed without a queue of its own: the wallet's nonce is taken as before. PENDING_SIGNATURE/awaiting_client_signature: Handed to the user's device (or MPC) to sign: what it signs comes back with the broadcast. PENDING_SIGNATURE/signing: Signed by Aurea for the wallet it holds the key of. SIGNED/signed_by_client: Signed on the user's side. SIGNED/signed_by_hub: Signed by Aurea. BROADCASTING/sending: Being handed to the chain's node, or to the provider. BROADCASTING/outcome_unknown: Handed over without an answer: it may still go through, and is never sent again by itself. CONFIRMING/awaiting_confirmation: On its way on chain, waiting for its receipt. CONFIRMING/awaiting_provider: Accepted by the provider, which has not settled it yet. CONFIRMING/awaiting_delivery: A swap mined on its source chain, which the router has not delivered yet (a cross-chain or intent swap; followed only where delivery tracking is switched on). CONFIRMING/awaiting_finalization: A Solana transaction the cluster confirmed, waiting to be finalized (followed only where the operations reconciliation runs); its answer and its transaction already say confirmed. CONFIRMING/confirming: Mined, and waiting until its chain has built the platform's confirmations for that chain on it (followed only where the confirmations are switched on). CONFIRMING/reorged: Its block left the chain in a reorganisation: the same signed transaction was handed to the node again, and it waits to be mined again. CONFIRMING/sped_up: Its transaction was replaced by the same one at the same nonce with a higher fee (POST /v1/operations/{id}/speed-up): whichever of them is mined ends it. COMPLETED/confirmed: Mined and successful. COMPLETED/processed: Settled by the provider. COMPLETED/signed: A signature, not a transaction: the message or digest is signed, and nothing is sent on chain. COMPLETED/delivered: A swap the router delivered as quoted. COMPLETED/delivered_other_token: A swap the router delivered in another token than the one quoted (a partial route). CANCELLING/drop_sent: A 0-value transaction to the wallet itself was sent at its transaction's nonce with a higher fee (POST /v1/operations/{id}/drop): CANCELLED if it is mined, COMPLETED or FAILED if the original is. FAILED/not_sent: Refused or failed before anything was signed or sent. FAILED/submission_failed: Sending it failed: the node or the provider refused it, or did not take it. FAILED/reverted: Mined, and reverted. FAILED/never_broadcast: Never signed and sent back within an hour: it can no longer be broadcast. FAILED/provider_rejected: Refused by the provider after it took the order. FAILED/delivery_failed: A swap mined on its source chain that the router reports failed on the way. FAILED/refunded: A swap the router could not deliver and refunded on the source chain. FAILED/approval_expired: Held for approval, and not approved within the approval window: nothing was signed or sent. FAILED/callback_expired: Held for the tenant's callback, which did not approve it before its deadline: nothing was signed or sent. FAILED/dropped: Its block left the chain in a reorganisation, and another transaction of the wallet took its nonce: it can never be mined.

get.description: The tenant's wallets, newest first, a page at a time: address, network, owner, who holds the key and the balances last read. Never key material. Filters: `kind`, `scheme`, `chain`, `status` (default: every wallet, active and deactivated), `network`, `userId`. `totals` counts every wallet of the tenant whatever the filters; `pagination.total` those the filters match. get.description: Your own active sessions, the most recently active first (at most 100): when each was signed in and last renewed, the device and address that last renewed it, and which one this request belongs to (`current`). A session ends when you sign out, when it is ended here, or when its refresh token expires. `tracked` is false when the platform keeps no server-side sessions: the list is then empty.

delete.description: Ends one of your own active sessions: its refresh token is refused from now on, and its access token where the platform checks sessions at each request. Ending the current one signs you out. 404 `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`: no active session of yours has this id.

post.description: Ends every active session of yours but the one this request belongs to, and says how many. 409 `SESSION_NOT_IDENTIFIED`: this request's access token names no session (the platform keeps no server-side sessions), so the others cannot be told apart from it.

get.description: The tenant's users, wallets, operations and volume, each for the last 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days with the period before, for the console's home and the tenant's overview. Read from what is recorded; nothing is read from a chain. The volume: COMPLETED operations of type TRANSFER, PAYOUT or SWAP with an amount above zero, created in the period, on the network asked for; summed per chain and asset in the asset's smallest unit (exact), and valued in EUR at the token registry's CURRENT price (the tenant's token, else the platform catalogue's price for the same symbol) — not the price at the operation's time. An asset the registry cannot price is never valued silently: it is listed with its amount in `unpricedAmount` and `unpricedAssets`, and the period says `partial`. A tenant's operators read their own tenant; Aurea's operators any tenant.

post.description: An EVM token contract added to the tenant's assets by its address: the Hub reads the contract on its chain (code, decimals(), symbol(), name()) through its own node and stores the asset with the contract's decimals — and its symbol and name unless the request names its own. Refused: no contract at the address (422 TOKEN_ADDRESS_NOT_A_CONTRACT), no ERC-20 decimals() (422 ASSET_NOT_ERC20), other decimals than the request names (422 ASSET_DECIMALS_MISMATCH, details.onChain), a wrong EIP-55 checksum (400 TOKEN_ADDRESS_CHECKSUM_INVALID), a chain the Hub does not support (400 ASSET_CHAIN_UNKNOWN) or one that is not EVM (400 ASSET_CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED), the node not answering (503 ASSET_CONTRACT_UNREAD, retryable), an asset the tenant lists already (409 ASSET_EXISTS, details.assetId) or a symbol another asset of the chain holds (409 ASSET_SYMBOL_TAKEN). The asset is then the tenant's as any token: its balances, sends and swaps read it — and, as with any token the tenant adds, on a chain where it listed none of its own the tenant's lists of that chain are its own from then on (the catalogue's are no longer used there: `source` says which). The tenant's operators, on their own tenant.

post.description: Verifies one of the tenant's users: a person (`kind: person`, KYC) or a company (`kind: company`, KYB), for a purpose (`bank_ramp`). 201 with a new verification, 200 with the live one (started, in review or verified: never a second one); a rejected or expired verification is replaced by a new one. Every change is sent as `identity.verification.updated`.

scope.description: platform: an operation with no tenant (Aurea's to decide).

reason.description: The decision's written reason (never in an event).

reason.description: Why it is PENDING: no_list, timeout or error.

post.summary: Validate an address for a chain
post.description: The address's format and checksum for the chain's family (EVM: EIP-55, absent when all one case; Solana: base58 of 32 bytes), and what sits there where it is cheap to know: an EVM address's code (one read of the tenant's node: eoa, contract, or an EIP-7702 delegated eoa; unknown when the node does not answer), a Solana address on the curve (a wallet) or off it (program-derived). In the body, so the address stays out of URLs and logs.

post.summary: Simulate a policy set on the tenant's history
post.description: Evaluates the set (a draft, or any version) on the tenant's operations of the last `days` (default 30, at most 90), the newest `limit` (default 2000, at most 5000): counts per verdict and per rule under the tenant's profile and under the institutional profile, with a sample of each rule's operations. Read only; amounts in EUR from the token registry (unknown when a price is missing). Changes nothing. The tenant's administrators, on their own tenant (a caller with no tenant is answered 400).

truncated.description: The window held more operations than the limit (the newest were evaluated), or the evaluation stopped at its time budget.

bySource.description: custodial_transaction (sent from a custodial wallet), prepared_transaction (handed to a client-side or MPC wallet to sign), gasless_permit, earn_operation, operation (recorded by the operations, with no transaction or prepared transaction of their own).

priced.description: Signatures whose amount was normalised to EUR.

unpriced.description: Signatures whose token or price is not known: their amount stays unknown to the engine (missing:amount).

addressBook.description: Present when the set names the destination kind address_book and the tenant's address book is in log or enforce: the signatures whose destination is an active entry of the book now (listed), and those whose destination is not (notListed). post.description: The tenant's approvers: the Approver, and the Owner, the Admin and the Non-signing Admin, on their own tenant. You generate a P-256 key pair and register its public key; the Hub never sees the private key. At most 2 active keys: to rotate, register the second, then revoke the first. **Signing a decision.** The approver keeps the private key of one of their approval keys and sends `signature`, a compact JWS signed ES256 (JOSE r‖s): header `{ "alg": "ES256", "typ": "aurea-approval+jwt", "kid": "<approval key id>" }` (no other member), payload the canonical payload's exact bytes, as `GET /v1/approvals/{operationId}` gives them in `payloads.approve` or `payloads.reject` — JSON with its members in this order and no whitespace: `{"action":"approve"|"reject","amount","approvalId","asset","chain","chainId","destination","expiresAt","operationId","ruleId","tenantId","v":1}`. A signature answers one request with one action, and is used once, ever. Refusals: 400 `APPROVAL_KEY_INVALID`, `APPROVAL_KEY_PRIVATE`, `APPROVAL_KEY_NAME_INVALID`; 409 `APPROVAL_KEY_IN_USE` (a key is registered once, ever), `APPROVAL_KEY_LIMIT`.

post.summary: Open a card onramp session for one of the user's wallets, or an address they proved
post.description: Creates a card onramp session that delivers pair's crypto to the destination named — walletId, one of the user's Aurea wallets whose key the Hub holds or has seen proven (a watch-only import is refused), or addressId, an address the user proved they control (POST /v1/ramp/card/addresses/verify) where the tenant allows it; exactly one of the two (400 CARD_ONRAMP_DESTINATION_INVALID otherwise). An EVM destination for an EVM network, a Solana one for Solana. The session is locked to that address and that network: the user cannot change either in the widget. sourceAmount (fiat, at most 2 decimals) or destinationAmount (crypto): in the first payment provider's widget only a suggestion the user can change, with the currency; in the second's (sessions that open only in the hosted page) the currency and a sourceAmount are fixed. The payment provider checks the user's country from the request's IP address and does the KYC, the payment and the delivery. Answers 201 with the session, the client secret and the publishable key to open the widget with — null where the payment provider's widget opens only in the hosted page (POST /v1/ramp/card/sessions/{id}/hosted-link). 403 CARD_ONRAMP_OFF where the tenant does not offer the onramp in that environment; 400 CARD_ONRAMP_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE (with details.available), CARD_ONRAMP_PAIR_NOT_SOLD_IN_CURRENCY when the pair is not sold in sourceCurrency (or the tenant's default currency) in that environment — each pair's sourceCurrencies in GET /config says where it is, with details.sourceCurrencies — CARD_ONRAMP_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED, CARD_ONRAMP_AMOUNT_INVALID; 404 CARD_ONRAMP_WALLET_NOT_FOUND or CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND; 403 CARD_ONRAMP_PROVEN_ADDRESSES_OFF for an addressId where the tenant does not allow proven addresses; and the payment provider's own refusals: 403 CARD_ONRAMP_CUSTOMER_UNSUPPORTED (this user's country cannot be served), 400 CARD_ONRAMP_INVALID_REQUEST, 503 CARD_ONRAMP_DISABLED / CARD_ONRAMP_MERCHANT_NOT_SET_UP / CARD_ONRAMP_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, 502 when the payment provider cannot be reached.

The same key with the same request answers the session it made, with a fresh client secret and idempotency-replayed: true, and the payment provider is not asked for a second one. The same key with a different request answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a key whose session the payment provider refused, 409 CARD_ONRAMP_SESSION_FAILED; a key that is not one, 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID. post.summary: A link to the hosted page for one of the user's open sessions
post.description: For an app without a web page of its own: open the answered `url` in a browser or an in-app browser. It shows the payment widget for the session with the tenant's name and logo, and after the session is paid, delivered or refused sends the browser to `returnUrl` with `onrampSession` and `status` added to its query. The link works for 30 minutes; its token is in the URL's fragment. `returnUrl` must be one of the tenant's allowed return URLs (400 RETURN_URL_NOT_ALLOWED otherwise, and always while the tenant allows none); without it, the page tells the user to close it. 409 CARD_ONRAMP_SESSION_CLOSED when the session is no longer initialized or requires_payment; 404 CARD_ONRAMP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND for another user's session; 400 CARD_ONRAMP_HOSTED_LINK_INVALID (with details.field) for a body with an unknown field, locale or theme.

post.summary: What the hosted page needs, for the link's token
post.description: Called by the hosted page itself, with the token of its link: the session's status, read again from the payment provider while it is not final, with what the user buys, for how much and where it goes (never an internal id); the client secret and publishable key while it can still be paid in the first provider's widget, or — with widget true — the URL of the second provider's widget, made for the address the request came from (single use, five minutes); where to send the browser back; the page's language and theme; the tenant's name and logo. 404 CARD_ONRAMP_LINK_NOT_FOUND for a token no link has, 410 CARD_ONRAMP_LINK_EXPIRED after 30 minutes, 403 CARD_ONRAMP_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED for a request a browser sends from another site, 400 CARD_ONRAMP_CUSTOMER_IP_REQUIRED when a widget is asked from no public address. At most 30 a minute per address.

post.summary: A challenge for proving one address the onramp may deliver to
post.description: Where the tenant allows it (GET /v1/ramp/card/config answers provenAddresses: true), a user may receive the crypto they buy at an address of their own wallet rather than an Aurea wallet — after proving they control it: ask for a challenge for the address, sign its message with the address's key (EIP-191 personal_sign on EVM, where the key controls the address on every EVM chain; ed25519 on Solana, the signature in base58), and send the signature to verify. A challenge lasts ten minutes, is used once, and is burnt after five wrong signatures; a user holds at most five open challenges. Answers 201 with the exact message to sign. 403 CARD_ONRAMP_OFF where the tenant does not offer the onramp, 403 CARD_ONRAMP_PROVEN_ADDRESSES_OFF where it does not allow proven addresses; 400 CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_INVALID (a mixed-case EVM address with a wrong checksum, the zero address, a Solana address that is not 32 bytes in base58); 409 CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_CHALLENGE_LIMIT with details.limit.

message.description: Sign exactly this text, line breaks included

post.summary: Keep the address a signed challenge proves
post.description: 201 with the proven address; 200 with it when the user already held it. 400 CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_SIGNATURE_INVALID (details.reason malformed or wrong_signer, details.attemptsLeft), CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_CHALLENGE_BURNT, CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_CHALLENGE_EXPIRED; 409 CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_CHALLENGE_USED; 404 CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_CHALLENGE_NOT_FOUND for a challenge that is not the user's; 403 CARD_ONRAMP_OFF or CARD_ONRAMP_PROVEN_ADDRESSES_OFF in the challenge's environment. label is the user's name for the address, up to 100 characters.

put.summary: Make, or read, the tenant's end user by its own id
put.description: For a tenant that holds its users' wallets and offers only the card onramp: its server names each end user by its own id (externalId: 1 to 100 letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons, @ or hyphens), attests the wallet the crypto goes to, and opens a session with the end user's IP address. The tenant's signed call is its statement that the wallet serves that user: no signature of the user is asked for. An end user needs no account: the first call that names an externalId makes it. 403 CARD_ONRAMP_TENANT_WALLETS_OFF until an Aurea administrator switched this on for the tenant in the environment, 403 CARD_ONRAMP_OFF where the card onramp is off; 401 for a missing, wrong, expired or replayed signature. Answers 201 the first time an externalId is named, 200 afterwards, with its wallets. Naming an end user is optional: the wallet and session calls make it too.

post.summary: Open a card purchase for the tenant's end user
post.description: Opens a session that delivers pair's crypto to the wallet named by address — attested by this call and kept as one of the end user's wallets — or, without address, to the end user's default wallet of the pair's family (PUT …/wallets/{family}); 409 CARD_ONRAMP_WALLET_MISSING when there is none. customerIp is the end user's public IP address: the payment provider decides from it whether it can serve the user (400 CARD_ONRAMP_CUSTOMER_IP_INVALID for a private, reserved or malformed one; 403 CARD_ONRAMP_CUSTOMER_UNSUPPORTED for a country it cannot serve). sourceAmount (fiat, at most 2 decimals) or destinationAmount: in the first payment provider's widget only a suggestion the user can change, with the currency; in the second's (sessions that open only in the hosted page) the currency and a sourceAmount are fixed. The session is locked to that wallet and that network. Answers 201 with the session, a hosted link to send the user to, and the client secret and publishable key to embed the widget instead (null where the payment provider's widget opens only in the hosted page); a replayed Idempotency-Key answers 200 with the same session and a fresh link. A return URL must be one the tenant allows (400 RETURN_URL_NOT_ALLOWED); the page sends the user there once the purchase is paid, delivered or refused, with from=onramp, onrampSession and status added. Also 400 CARD_ONRAMP_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE, CARD_ONRAMP_PAIR_NOT_SOLD_IN_CURRENCY (the pair is not sold in sourceCurrency, or the tenant's default currency, in that environment: details.sourceCurrencies names where it is), CARD_ONRAMP_AMOUNT_INVALID, CARD_ONRAMP_ADDRESS_INVALID, CARD_ONRAMP_CUSTOMER_ID_INVALID. For a tenant that holds its users' wallets and offers only the card onramp: its server names each end user by its own id (externalId: 1 to 100 letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons, @ or hyphens), attests the wallet the crypto goes to, and opens a session with the end user's IP address. The tenant's signed call is its statement that the wallet serves that user: no signature of the user is asked for. An end user needs no account: the first call that names an externalId makes it. 403 CARD_ONRAMP_TENANT_WALLETS_OFF until an Aurea administrator switched this on for the tenant in the environment, 403 CARD_ONRAMP_OFF where the card onramp is off; 401 for a missing, wrong, expired or replayed signature.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Optional. Up to 255 letters, digits, - or _. The same key with the same request answers the session it made, with a fresh client secret and idempotency-replayed: true, and the payment provider is not asked for a second one. Every other check is made before a key is replayed.

get.summary: The earn products the tenant offers
get.description: The products the tenant switched on for the network, each with its state and rate on every chain it is on, read now: `observedAt` is when they were true and `fresh` whether a deposit or a withdrawal may be decided on them. A product not switched on is not listed.

parameters.name: isTestnet
parameters.description: The network: `true` testnet, `false` (the default) mainnet.

readable.description: False when the chain could not be read.

state.description: The product's state on chain: active; frozen (withdrawals only); paused or inactive (nothing).

observedAt.description: When the state and the rate were true (the block's time).

fresh.description: Whether the reading is recent enough for a deposit or a withdrawal to be decided on it.

422.description: Default Response

get.summary: A product's disclosure, before the first deposit
get.description: The product's current disclosure — its risks, and that its yield is variable and read at the time stated with the product — and whether the user accepted it. A deposit needs the current version accepted (409 `EARN_DISCLOSURE_NOT_ACCEPTED`); a product whose disclosure is not published takes no deposit (409 `EARN_DISCLOSURE_NOT_PUBLISHED`).

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Two-letter language code; the English text when there is none in this language.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The product's identifier, for example `lumen` or `stablecoin-savings-usdc`.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of `body`: send it back with the acceptance.

accepted.description: Whether the user accepted this version.

422.description: Default Response

post.description: Records that the user accepted the disclosure they were shown: its version, language and the `sha256` the disclosure route answered. Not the current text: 409 `EARN_DISCLOSURE_VERSION_MISMATCH`. Accepting again answers the first acceptance (200).

language.description: Two-letter language code; the English text when there is none in this language.

get.summary: What the user holds in the earn products
get.description: For every product the tenant offers on the network and every EVM wallet of the user somebody can sign for: the position's value, principal and yield together, read from the chain. Positions of zero are left out.

parameters.name: isTestnet
parameters.description: The network: `true` testnet, `false` (the default) mainnet.

balance.description: What the position is worth now, principal and yield, in the smallest unit.

shares.description: A vault product: the share tokens the position is made of, valued in `balance` at the product's exit price.

incomplete.description: True when a chain could not be read: the list may miss a position.

422.description: Default Response

get.summary: What a deposit or a withdrawal would do
get.description: The same checks as the write, then what it would do: the route, who signs, the wallet, the amount expected, the fee, what the wallet or the position holds and the exact approval a deposit needs first. The reading's age and the chain's state are answered, not refused. The tenant must offer the product on the network (403 `EARN_PRODUCT_OFF`; an unknown product is 404 `EARN_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`). A product the tenant switched off, or that is paused, takes no new deposit; a withdrawal of a position goes on.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The product's identifier, for example `lumen` or `stablecoin-savings-usdc`.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: In the smallest unit; a withdrawal may say "max".

parameters.name: isTestnet
parameters.description: The network: `true` testnet, `false` (the default) mainnet.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: The route to quote; without it, the first open to the wallet.

parameters.description: The chain to quote on; without it, the one the wallet is on.

signer.description: Who signs: the Hub (custodial wallet) or the client (device or MPC).

amount.description: Null: the whole position.

available.description: The wallet's balance of the asset (deposit) or the position (withdrawal).

approvalAmount.description: The exact approval a deposit needs first, or null.

readable.description: False when the chain could not be read.

state.description: The product's state on chain: active; frozen (withdrawals only); paused or inactive (nothing).

observedAt.description: When the state and the rate were true (the block's time).

fresh.description: Whether the reading is recent enough for a deposit or a withdrawal to be decided on it.

shares.description: A vault product: the share tokens the operation adds (deposit) or takes (withdrawal).

nativeFee.description: The bridge route: the fee paid with the transaction, in the chain's native token's smallest unit (the router keeps all of it).

422.description: Default Response

post.description: Deposits `amount` of the product's asset from one of the user's wallets. The approval, when one is needed, is of exactly the amount, never more. The tenant's limits apply (400 `EARN_AMOUNT_OUT_OF_LIMITS`), the product must take deposits (409 `EARN_PRODUCT_PAUSED`) and the wallet hold the amount (400 `EARN_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`). The user must have accepted the product's current disclosure: 409 `EARN_DISCLOSURE_NOT_PUBLISHED` while none is published, 409 `EARN_DISCLOSURE_NOT_ACCEPTED` (with its `version`) until then — read it with GET /v1/earn/products/{productId}/disclosure and accept it with POST /v1/earn/products/{productId}/disclosure/acceptances; a withdrawal never waits for it. The tenant must offer the product on the network (403 `EARN_PRODUCT_OFF`; an unknown product is 404 `EARN_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`). A product the tenant switched off, or that is paused, takes no new deposit; a withdrawal of a position goes on. A custodial wallet: the Hub signs and sends the steps at once and answers the operation completed, failed, or broadcast when a receipt is late. A client-side or MPC wallet: the operation is answered submitted with `signing.steps`; sign each `txHashToSign` and send the signatures to POST /v1/earn/operations/{operationId}/broadcast. Before anything is built, the product's state and rate are read again: older than the Hub's limit, 503 `EARN_READING_STALE`; not taking the operation on chain, 409 `EARN_PRODUCT_NOT_ACCEPTING`; unreadable, 503 `EARN_READING_FAILED`. A wallet: `walletId`, or the first one somebody can sign for (404 `EARN_WALLET_NOT_FOUND`, 400 `EARN_WALLET_NOT_SIGNABLE` for a watch-only address, 400 `EARN_NO_WALLET`).

Without it, the first of these open to the wallet. A route not open to it is refused (409 `EARN_ROUTE_NOT_OFFERED`).

chainId.description: The chain to operate on, by its id. Without it, the one the wallet is on. A chain the product is not on is refused (400 `EARN_CHAIN_NOT_OFFERED`).

parameters.description: Optional. Up to 255 letters, digits, - or _. post.description: The signatures of an operation answered submitted, one per step, in order: each is checked against the operation's wallet (422 `EARN_SIGNATURE_INVALID`; a count that does not match, 400 `EARN_SIGNATURES_MISMATCH`), the product is read again (as for the write), then the steps are sent exactly as they were built. Once a step is out, the answer is the operation in the state it reached.

get.summary: The tokenized assets the tenant offers
get.description: Tokenized shares, ETFs, portfolios and the tokens that settle them, as the tenant offers them in the environment: the product lines it switched on, every asset of them or the ones it selected, without the assets for professional investors only while it keeps them out. Sorted by symbol, byte by byte (upper case before lower case). The query is checked before the access token and the signature: a value its schema refuses (isTestnet, productLine, a limit or offset out of range) answers 400, with the list of problems in `details`; a chainId other than 1 or 56 answers 422 after the gate. A tenant without tokenized assets set up in the environment is answered 403 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_NOT_CONFIGURED`; set up but not offering them there, 403 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_OFF`. Contact us for details: https://www.aureahub.com/contact

post.description: Carries out one of the user's binding quotes (status `attested`) exactly as it was signed, within its validity. A wallet its owner signs for needs a long quote (409 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_QUOTE_TOO_SHORT`); use a limit order otherwise. A wallet Aurea signs for is signed and sent at once (`txHash`); a wallet its owner signs for gets the transaction to sign (`requiresClientSigning`, `txHashToSign`, `preparedTxId`) and sends the signature to /broadcast — on Solana the message to sign (`messageToSign`), sent to /broadcast-solana. The secondary route: offered only by a tenant that switched it on (else 403 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_SECONDARY_ROUTE_OFF`), in production only (409 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_SECONDARY_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE`), with the same eligibility and documents as the primary route (403) and refused while the asset is paused (409 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_ASSET_PAUSED`). A tenant without tokenized assets set up in the environment is answered 403 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_NOT_CONFIGURED`; set up but not offering them there, 403 `TOKENIZED_ASSETS_OFF`. Contact us for details: https://www.aureahub.com/contact

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Optional (required for institutional tenants). Up to 255 letters, digits, - or _. Sending the same key again with the same request answers with the first answer instead of running it again, and the response carries idempotency-replayed: true. The same key with a different request, or while the first call is still running, answers 409 with details.code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED or IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS; after a first call that may have taken effect without answering, 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (it is never run again: check the operation, then use a new key). A key that is not one answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID. A request without the header behaves as it always has. Keys last 24 hours.

parameters.name: x-external-tx-id
parameters.description: Optional. Your own id for the operation this call starts: up to 255 letters, digits, and - _ . : — unique for your tenant for ever. The operation keeps it (externalTxId) and GET /v1/operations/by-external-id/{externalTxId} finds it. An id another operation of your tenant already holds answers 409 with details.code EXTERNAL_TX_ID_REUSED and details.operationId, before anything is signed or sent; an id that is not one answers 400 EXTERNAL_TX_ID_INVALID. A call refused before it recorded an operation (a validation error, say) leaves the id free. With an Idempotency-Key, the same key and the same id answer the first answer again. Honoured once Aurea records your operations (GET /v1/operations lists them); until then the header is not read. A request without it behaves as it always has.

post.summary: Consent to an external AI agent
post.description: The signed-in user consents to an external AI agent (`clientName`) calling the MCP tools with `scopes` (each one a permission the user holds), optionally pinned to one `agentId`, for `expiresInDays` (at most the platform's maximum). Without `codeChallenge`, answers the grant and its token (`amcp_…`) once. With a PKCE `codeChallenge` (S256) and optionally a `redirectUri` (https, or a loopback http address) and `state`, answers a one-time `code` (10 minutes) the client exchanges at POST /mcp/token with its verifier, and the `redirectTo` address to send the user back to.

post.summary: Freeze a user or a wallet of the tenant
post.description: The tenant's Owner, Admin and Security Admin, on their own tenant (Aurea administrators on any): its users (never one's own account, never a platform account) and its wallets; never the tenant itself. In force on every instance when this answers (it waits about a second after writing): a frozen tenant answers 423 `TENANT_FROZEN` to every authenticated request of its users and to its API key, a frozen user 423 `USER_FROZEN` to every authenticated request, and a frozen wallet 423 `WALLET_FROZEN` at every signing point and in the MPC relay (a wallet is its address in its tenant: every chain's row of it); a frozen `account` 423 `ACCOUNT_FROZEN` there for every wallet it holds (a user's default account: the user's wallets that are in no account). 404 `FREEZE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`, 409 `ALREADY_FROZEN`, 403 `FREEZE_SELF`, 400 `FREEZE_UNTIL_PAST`.

post.summary: Register a server credential (a public key)
post.description: The tenant's Owner, Admin, Non-signing Admin and Security Admin, on their own tenant (Aurea administrators on any). The tenant generates a P-256 key pair and registers its public key; the Hub never sees the private key. Several credentials may be active at once (at most 10): to rotate, register the new key, move the server to it, revoke the old one. **Signing with a credential.** The tenant's server keeps the private key and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, a compact JWS signed ES256 (JOSE r‖s signature): header `{ "alg": "ES256", "typ": "aurea-server+jwt", "kid": "<credential id>" }` (no other member); claims `{ "uri": "<METHOD> <path and query exactly as sent>", "bodyHash": "<unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the exact body; of the empty string without one>", "nonce": "<16–128 of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ -, never reused>", "iat": <seconds>, "exp": <seconds> }`, with `exp` after `iat` by 30 s at most (clock skew allowed: 10 s). It is accepted, instead of the HMAC headers (never with them: 400 `SERVER_AUTH_SCHEMES_CONFLICT`), on every route that takes the tenant's signature alone: sign-up and sign-in, `GET /v1/tenant/public`, the MPC service token, the card ramp's customers. Refusals are 401 with `details.code`: `SERVER_TOKEN_MALFORMED`, `SERVER_TOKEN_LIFETIME_INVALID`, `SERVER_TOKEN_NOT_YET_VALID`, `SERVER_TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_UNKNOWN`, `SERVER_TOKEN_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_REVOKED`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRED`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_TENANT_INACTIVE`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `SERVER_TOKEN_URI_MISMATCH`, `SERVER_TOKEN_BODY_MISMATCH`, `SERVER_TOKEN_REPLAYED`. A credential whose role narrows (`roleNarrows`) and does not hold the route's permission is refused 403 `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED`, with the permission in `details.permission` and in the challenge's `scope`. Refusals: 400 `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_KEY_INVALID`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_PRIVATE_KEY`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_NAME_INVALID`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_ROLE_INVALID`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_IP_INVALID`, `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRY_INVALID`; 403 `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_ROLE_ABOVE_OWN`, `TEST_ONLY_CREDENTIALS_OFF`; 404 `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`; 409 `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_KEY_IN_USE` (a key is registered once, ever), `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_LIMIT`.

role.description: The tenant role the credential carries: tenantadmin, non_signing_admin, signer, approver, editor, viewer, auditor, security_admin, security_auditor — within the caller's own (403 `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_ROLE_ABOVE_OWN`). It reaches no permissioned route: a token reaches the routes the tenant's signature reaches. A credential registered since 06/10/2026 (`roleNarrows: true`) reaches only the tenant-signed routes whose permission its role holds: `GET /v1/tenant/public` every role; sign-up and sign-in (`/v1/auth/register`, `/login`, `/google`, `/apple`, `/forgot-password`) `tenant.users.write` (Admin, Non-signing Admin); `POST /v1/mpc/service/token` and the card ramp's customers (`/v1/ramp/card/customers/*`) `self.mpc.use` and `self.card_ramp.use` (Admin, Signer).

publicKey.description: The credential's P-256 public key as a JWK: `{ "kty": "EC", "crv": "P-256", "x": "…", "y": "…" }` (`x`, `y`: 32 bytes each, unpadded base64url). `alg` ("ES256"), `use` ("sig"), `kid`, `key_ops` and `ext` are accepted and dropped. Never the private key: a JWK with `d` is refused (400 `SERVER_CREDENTIAL_PRIVATE_KEY`).

allowedIps.description: IPv4 or IPv6 networks (`203.0.113.0/24`, `2001:db8::/32`, or a bare address), at most 50; matched against the address the API sees the call come from. Empty or left out: any address.

expiresAt.description: When its tokens stop being accepted: in the future, at most 5 years ahead. Null or left out: no expiry.

testOnly.description: Optional. `true`: a credential for test networks only — its tokens reach a route only when the request names a testnet — `isTestnet: true` in the query or body, and every `chainId` it carries a testnet's. A request for a mainnet, and a route that does not take the network from the request (sign-up and sign-in, `GET /v1/tenant/public`, the MPC service token, a record read or acted on by its id), answer 403 `TEST_ONLY_CREDENTIAL` with `details.network` (`mainnet` or `undetermined`); nothing is done and the token's nonce is not used. Only where test-only credentials are switched on for the tenant, else 403 `TEST_ONLY_CREDENTIALS_OFF`. Left out or `false`: a credential as every other.

get.description: Which rail serves the signed-in user's USD and, on the USD account, everything about it: its `status`, `capabilities`, the `requirements` still open, the USD bank details per rail (ACH, Fedwire, SWIFT: one each, ready once collections are active), the balances and the custody mode. Always 200: the next step of a blocked state is in `nextStep` (for `bank_ramp`: use_bank_ramp, the bank ramp's pay-in routes with fiatCurrency USD; for `none`: the rail router's next step). `custody` (optional) asks the router for that custody mode instead of the account's or the tenant's default. Changes are sent to the tenant as `ramp.account.updated`. Answers 404 while Aurea has not switched USD accounts on.

put.summary: Choose the USD account's custody mode
put.description: `custodial`: USD received stays on the account and payouts leave from it; `self_custody`: USD received goes on to the customer's Aurea wallet as a stablecoin. Only a mode the rail router allows for the customer (else 409 with next step choose_custody and the modes allowed). The rail router decides per customer: `usd_account` serves these routes; for `bank_ramp` they answer 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_EXISTING_RAIL` (next step use_bank_ramp) and for `none` 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_RAIL_UNAVAILABLE` with the next step. The account must be open (`active`) with the capability the operation needs, else 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_ACCOUNT_NOT_READY` with the account's `status` and next step. Answers 404 while Aurea has not switched USD accounts on.

post.summary: Pay out USD from the account
post.description: Pays `amount` USD (two decimals, at least 100) to an `active` beneficiary (`beneficiaryId` from GET /v1/ramp/bank/customer/beneficiaries) from the account's balance; answered as a withdrawal with purpose `customer_account` and sent to the tenant as `ramp.withdrawal.updated`. No costs configured for the tenant here: 409 `BANK_RAMP_COSTS_NOT_CONFIGURED` (next step contact_support). The tenant's 24-hour limits apply as to every withdrawal. The tenant's policy, approvals, screening and Travel Rule apply as to every payout; a third-party beneficiary needs `invoiceDocumentId`. When Aurea requires a passkey step-up for money out, send the user's `bank_ramp.payout` step-up token in `x-aurea-step-up` (403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`); a replay of an answered Idempotency-Key needs none. The rail router decides per customer: `usd_account` serves these routes; for `bank_ramp` they answer 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_EXISTING_RAIL` (next step use_bank_ramp) and for `none` 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_RAIL_UNAVAILABLE` with the next step. The account must be open (`active`) with the capability the operation needs, else 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_ACCOUNT_NOT_READY` with the account's `status` and next step. Answers 404 while Aurea has not switched USD accounts on.

travelRule.description: IVMS 101 data where the Travel Rule asks for it (as on every bank ramp payout).

get.summary: One of the USD account's payouts
get.description: `receiptUrl` once it completed. 404 `BANK_RAMP_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` when it is not the account's. The rail router decides per customer: `usd_account` serves these routes; for `bank_ramp` they answer 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_EXISTING_RAIL` (next step use_bank_ramp) and for `none` 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_RAIL_UNAVAILABLE` with the next step. The account must be open (`active`) with the capability the operation needs, else 409 `BANK_RAMP_USD_ACCOUNT_NOT_READY` with the account's `status` and next step. Answers 404 while Aurea has not switched USD accounts on.

post.summary: Upload a document the USD account asks for
post.description: The file is the body (application/pdf, image/png or image/jpeg, 5 MB at most); `type` must be one of the `documentTypes` a requirement of GET /v1/ramp/bank/customer/accounts lists (`partyId` for an owner's requirement, `side` front or back for a two-sided document), else 400 `BANK_RAMP_VERIFICATION_DOCUMENT_INVALID`. The file is passed on and never kept by Aurea; the account is read again and answered as GET /v1/ramp/bank/customer/accounts answers it, without its bank details and balances (empty here: read them there). Answers 404 while Aurea has not switched USD accounts on.

nextStep.description: The button a client shows, null when nothing is asked. complete_verification: finish the identity verification; provide_proof_of_address: upload a proof of address; operator_review: Aurea reviews the customer's residence (wait, or contact support); contact_support: help@aureahub.com; choose_custody: pick one of custodyOptions (PUT …/accounts/custody); open_account: send the profile (PUT /v1/ramp/bank/customer/profile) and open the account; provide_information / upload_document (POST /v1/ramp/bank/customer/verification/documents) / accept_terms (GET /v1/ramp/bank/customer/terms): what the account's requirements ask; wait_for_review: the bank ramp reviews; use_bank_ramp: USD stays on POST /v1/ramp/bank/payin/initiate (fiatCurrency USD) and the payout routes; use_usd_account: USD goes through GET /v1/ramp/bank/customer/accounts.
